page.layout: One printed page: running head at top; a heading line "Auis rupta cauea euadens" with number XV at right; below it a woodcut illustration (engraving of a room with a broken birdcage); below the picture a four-line verse with a large initial L; at the foot a catchword "Nauis".

main_text.head: Auis rupta cauea euadens. XV.

p.i: [Woodcut illustration: a room with a broken birdcage and a bird escaping; described under notes.]

main_text.p: Libera ceu Volucris, cauea mox carcere clausa,

p.i: Liber homo natus, mortis dein clausus in antro,
Rursus abit Christo liber ad astra duce.

page.notes: The woodcut shows an interior with a wooden birdcage, its door broken open, a bird flying out, and a second cage at right; the floor is drawn with hatching. The initial L of the verse is a large woodcut letter, read as L. Catchword "Nauis" is printed at the foot right.
